note: Recherche documentaire : catalogues de serveurs MCP et de plugins, signaux de classement, contrôles de sécurité, commandes d’installation. Chaque ligne porte sa source et sa fiabilité.

rows.name: Official MCP Registry (modelcontextprotocol)
rows.what: The official, centralised metadata registry for publicly accessible MCP servers, backed by Anthropic, GitHub, PulseMCP and Microsoft. Each entry is a server.json record with a reverse-DNS name (io.github.user/server or com.example/server), a description, a version, a repository, and either packages (npm, pypi, nuget, cargo, oci, mcpb) or remotes (streamable-http, sse). The registry has been in preview since 2025-09-08, and breaking changes or data resets may still occur. It publishes no total count. Third-party counts, reported only: 30,375 servers (99,114 version records) on 2026-09-10, and 52,042 latest-version servers on 2026-10-28 via the API. These figures depend on whether you count latest versions or all version records.
rows.access: Base URL: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io. It needs no authentication and is read-only. Use API v0.1, which has been frozen since 2025-10-24; v0 still changes. Endpoints: GET /v0.1/servers, GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions and GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions/{version}. The version can be 'latest', and path parameters must be URL-encoded. Query parameters: limit, cursor (taken from metadata.nextCursor), updated_since (RFC 3339), search (matches a substring of the name, with no ranking), and version=latest. Without version=latest, the list returns every version of every server. Tested today with GET /v0.1/servers?limit=1&search=io.github.github/github-mcp-server&version=latest, which returned HTTP 200. The entry held $schema (2025-12-11), name, title, description, repository.url, version 2.1.0, packages[] (registryType oci, identifier ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:2.1.0, transport stdio, runtimeArguments with variables marked isSecret), remotes[] (streamable-http https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ with headers) and _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/official'] {status, statusChangedAt, publishedAt, updatedAt, isLatest}. The rate limit was not found, because the test returned no rate-limit headers. The maximum page size was not tested. The docs recommend doing an initial full crawl once, then running incremental syncs with updated_since about once an hour, using compression and backoff. Incremental results include servers whose status changed to deprecated or deleted.
rows.signals: Popularity: none. The registry is deliberately unopinionated and leaves ratings to aggregators. Trust: namespace authentication proves control of the GitHub account or the domain (through GitHub OAuth or OIDC, a DNS challenge or an HTTP challenge). Package ownership is verified per type: mcpName in package.json for npm, an 'mcp-name:' string in the README for PyPI, NuGet and Cargo, the OCI label io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name, and a fileSha256 for mcpb. Each record has a status field (active, deprecated or deleted); 'deleted' usually means moderation removed it as spam or malware. Freshness: publishedAt, updatedAt and statusChangedAt. A record also shows whether the server is remote or local, through remotes[] versus packages[]. Categories and tags: none. Security scanning is delegated to the package registries and to downstream aggregators.
rows.terms: No data licence or terms of use for the metadata were found. The repository LICENSE covers code (Apache-2.0, with some older parts MIT) and documentation (CC-BY-4.0), not the server metadata. The aggregators guide explicitly intends the data for downstream aggregators, which scrape it and persist it in their own store. The registry gives no uptime or data-durability guarantee.
rows.install: Each record is machine-readable install data. For npm with runtimeHint npx, run 'npx -y <identifier>'. For PyPI, run 'uvx <identifier>'. For NuGet, run 'dnx'. For Cargo, run 'cargo install' and then call the binary by name. For OCI, run 'docker run'. For mcpb, verify fileSha256 before installing. Remotes give a URL plus headers. For Claude Code, verified today: 'claude mcp add --transport stdio <name> --env KEY=VALUE -- <command> [args]', 'claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> --header "Authorization: Bearer ..."', 'claude mcp add-json <name> '<json>'', and the scopes '--scope local|project|user'. Project scope writes .mcp.json. Also 'claude mcp list', 'claude mcp get' and 'claude mcp remove <name>'. Commands for other agents: not found in this research.
rows.notes: This registry is the best backbone, because it is open, needs no key, uses a standard schema and supports incremental sync. It has no popularity data, so ranking needs a join with GitHub stars (via repository.url), npm or PyPI downloads (via packages[].identifier), or Docker pull_count. Verified risk: entries under the ai.smithery/* namespace point to server.smithery.ai and require a Smithery Bearer key. For example, ai.smithery/Hint-Services-obsidian-github-mcp is still status=active and isLatest=true. The Smithery /future page says server.smithery.ai URLs stopped working on 2026-10-31. The catalogue build should therefore filter out remotes on server.smithery.ai and run.tools. The registry OpenAPI spec lets sub-registries inject their own data under _meta, with a namespaced key such as 'com.example.subregistry/custom'.

rows.name: GitHub MCP Registry (github.com/mcp)
rows.what: GitHub's curated MCP server directory, which acts as a sub-registry of the official MCP Registry. Tested today, it holds 771 servers in total (metadata.total = 771). The web page sorts them by GitHub stars in descending order; its first entry, microsoft/markitdown, shows 195,222, which equals the API's stargazerCount. Each card shows a logo, a name, a publisher, a one-line description, the star count and an Install button.
rows.access: Tested today with GET https://api.mcp.github.com/v0.1/servers?limit=1, which returned HTTP 200 without a key. The endpoint follows the v0.1 registry shape and adds metadata {count, nextCursor, per_page, total, total_pages}. The cursor encodes the star count, so pages come in star order. Fields of one entry: server.name ('microsoft/markitdown'), description, version, repository {id, source, url}, packages[] (registryType pypi, identifier markitdown-mcp, runtimeHint uvx, transport stdio) and _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided'].github. That github object holds stargazerCount, license ('MIT License'), topics[], primaryLanguage, isInOrganization, pushedAt, ownerAvatarUrl, displayName and readme (the full README text). The entry also has _meta official {status, publishedAt, updatedAt, isLatest}. The host api.mcp.github.com has no public documentation, so it may change without notice. Rate limit: not found.
rows.signals: Popularity: stargazerCount. Trust: the list is curated by GitHub and small (771 servers). isInOrganization shows whether the repository belongs to an organisation. Each entry carries a licence and a status. Freshness: pushedAt (the last push to the repository), readmeUpdatedAt and updatedAt. Topics can serve as tags. Remote or local is visible from remotes[] versus packages[].
rows.terms: No terms specific to this API were found. The web page links to the general GitHub Terms of Service. Reuse terms for the data: not found.
rows.install: Same as the official registry: the packages[] and remotes[] data map to install commands. The web Install button targets clients that this research did not establish. GitHub documents that Copilot can use a registry URL as an enterprise allowlist, and that Copilot appends /v0.1 to it itself.
rows.notes: Use this as the shortlist of the best servers, with stars, licence, topics and README already joined in, all from a single source with no key. The endpoint was tested but is undocumented, so treat it as unstable.

rows.name: Smithery (now part of Arcade)
rows.what: An MCP server registry and hosting proxy. Tested today, it lists 20,750 servers (pagination.totalCount = 20750). Its /future page says that on 2026-10-31 Smithery shut down its server URLs on run.tools and server.smithery.ai, the Smithery API, Connect and Toolbox, accounts and API keys, and the CLI and SDKs. It says it will continue as a public, non-proxied MCP registry: the smithery.ai directory, now powered by Arcade.dev, with a curated set of verified servers that show direct MCP URLs.
rows.access: Tested today: GET https://registry.smithery.ai/servers?pageSize=1 and GET https://api.smithery.ai/servers?pageSize=1 both returned HTTP 200 without a key, even though the /future page lists the API as shut down. List fields: id, qualifiedName, namespace, displayName, description, iconUrl, verified, useCount, remote, isDeployed, unlisted, inactive, createdAt, homepage, bySmithery, owner and score (null in the test), plus pagination {currentPage, pageSize, totalPages (500), totalCount}. Tested GET https://api.smithery.ai/servers/brave, which returned remote, deploymentUrl (https://brave.run.tools), connections[] with a JSON Schema in configSchema, security (null), and tools[] with inputSchema. Reported by secondary sources: a semantic search parameter q, filters such as is:deployed, owner: and repo:, and Bearer authentication. The documentation pages returned 404 today. Rate limit: not found.
rows.signals: Popularity: useCount (87,579 for Brave Search in the test). Trust: verified, bySmithery, and remote or isDeployed. Freshness: only createdAt was seen. The detail record has a 'security' field, which was null in the test. The tool list is useful for search.
rows.terms: Not found: smithery.ai/terms returned 404, and the /tos and /terms-of-service pages redirect to a 'Not found' page.
rows.install: Historically Smithery offered a CLI and hosted URLs, which have been deprecated or shut down since 2026-10-31. The detail record's configSchema could still help build environment prompts. To connect, use the vendor's direct MCP URL, which the /future page says is shown on each server page.
rows.notes: Do not use Smithery as a backbone. Its API is officially shut down and could stop at any moment. Its terms are missing. Its hosted URLs are dead, and these dead URLs also appear in official registry entries under the ai.smithery/* namespace. At most, use useCount as an optional, best-effort extra popularity signal while the endpoint still answers.

rows.name: Glama MCP directory
rows.what: The largest directory found. Its page showed 120,628 servers on 2026-11-13, sourced from community submissions, automated discovery with manual curation, the official registry and awesome-mcp-servers. Attribute counts on the page: Remote 47,366, Local 45,816 and Hybrid 22,579; Official 8,092 and Claimed 11,402; Python 50,437 and TypeScript 41,168. There are many categories. Each server has letter grades from A to D for licence, quality and maintenance.
rows.access: Base URL: https://glama.ai/api/mcp. Its endpoints list servers, list attributes, get one server, list remote connectors, list hosted instances, and accept telemetry. Tested today: GET https://glama.ai/api/mcp/v1/servers?first=1 returned HTTP 401 'This endpoint requires an API key', so a Bearer key from a Glama account is required. Pagination is a cursor (pass endCursor as 'after' until hasNextPage is false). Rate limit: 100 requests per second per IP, with RateLimit-* headers; repeated 429s can lead to a permanent 403. The field list of a server object was not found, because the reference page did not show it.
rows.signals: Sorting by Recent Usage, Weekly npm Downloads, Weekly PyPI Downloads, GitHub Stars, Recent GitHub Stars, Date Added and Date Updated. Trust: the official, claimed and hosting attributes, plus the licence, quality and maintenance grades. The cards show no separate security grade, although a security category exists. Glama score badges appear on many entries in awesome-mcp-servers.
rows.terms: The API Data License is section 15 of the terms, effective 2026-08-25, and the terms as a whole are effective 2026-08-27. It is a limited, revocable licence that requires an API key. Every page that shows Glama data must visibly credit Glama with a link, and each record must link to its Glama listing. It forbids bulk redistribution, building a product that competes with the Glama directory, and embedding a key in a publicly distributed client. Cached data must be deleted within 30 days of termination.
rows.install: Not found in this research.
rows.notes: Glama is unsuitable as the data source for a free public catalogue. It needs an account and key, a public client may not embed that key, it forbids competing directories, and it forbids bulk republication. At most, a link to a server's Glama page could be shown.

rows.name: PulseMCP
rows.what: An MCP server directory that showed 21,552 servers today. It sorts by Most Popular (all time, this month or this week), Recently Released and Last Updated. Its filters are Remote Available and a classification of Anthropic References, Official Providers or Community. New submissions are currently paused. It also offers a Sub-Registry API that implements the generic registry API with its own extensions.
rows.access: Tested today: GET https://api.pulsemcp.com/v0beta/servers returned HTTP 410 API_SUNSET, because v0beta was fully retired in September 2026. GET https://api.pulsemcp.com/v0.1/servers?limit=1 returned HTTP 401 'Invalid or missing API key' (the X-API-Key header). The docs also require an X-Tenant-ID header and describe the service as a 'private B2B integration'; keys are requested by email. Endpoints follow the v0.1 registry shape, with limit from 1 to 100, cursor, updated_since, search and version=latest. Rate limits: 200 requests per minute, 5,000 per hour and 10,000 per day.
rows.signals: Under _meta['com.pulsemcp/server']: visitorsEstimateMostRecentWeek, visitorsEstimateLastFourWeeks and visitorsEstimateTotal, updated weekly and partly derived from public download counts, plus isOfficial (the maintainer owns the service it integrates with). The version-level _meta has status, publishedAt and updatedAt. Premium fields: isSelfHosted, authOptions and tools. Security scans are marked 'Coming Soon'.
rows.terms: Not found. The docs say to contact the company by email.
rows.install: Not applicable: PulseMCP holds metadata only.
rows.notes: Not usable without a partner agreement. isOfficial would be a valuable trust signal, but no open source for it was found.

rows.name: mcp.so
rows.what: An independent community directory. Its page, updated 2026-11-13, showed 20,399 MCP servers (1,409 of them remote), 394 clients, 268 agent skills and 177 CLI tools. It has categories (Developer Tools, AI & Agents, Cloud & Infrastructure, Memory & Knowledge, Media & Design, and others), a 'Featured' label, an 'Official' label on CLI tools, and sorting by featured, star (trending) or latest.
rows.access: No API or data export was found; the site only links to a feed.
rows.signals: Featured status, stars or trending, date and category. Download counts and verification: not found.
rows.terms: Terms last updated 2026.07.01. They state that the service's original content is owned by mcp.so and protected by copyright, and they forbid disrupting the service. No permission to reuse data was found.
rows.install: Not found.
rows.notes: Not suitable as a data source, because it has no API and its terms are restrictive.

rows.name: Docker MCP Catalog (Docker Hub mcp namespace and docker/mcp-registry)
rows.what: Docker's curated catalogue of containerised MCP servers. The docs say it has '300+' servers. Tested today, the docker/mcp-registry GitHub repository has 327 entries in its servers/ folder, with the last commit on 2026-11-10. The Docker Hub 'mcp' namespace has 244 repositories, which are the Docker-built images. Option A, recommended: Docker builds, signs and publishes the image with provenance and an SBOM. Option B: the author supplies a pre-built image. Remote and partner servers are also mentioned.
rows.access: Tested today: GET https://hub.docker.com/v2/namespaces/mcp/repositories?page_size=2 returned HTTP 200 without a key, with count 244. Fields: name, description, star_count, pull_count (1,990,466 for mcp/fetch), last_updated, date_registered and categories. The catalogue source data comes from the GitHub repository at servers/<name>/server.yaml; the GitHub contents API worked without a key, with its limit of 60 requests per hour. Sample github-official/server.yaml fields: name, image (ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server), type, meta.category (devops), meta.tags, about {title, description, icon}, source {project, commit}, run.allowHosts (a network allowlist), config.secrets[] {name, env, example, description} and oauth[]. The Docker Hub API rate limit was not checked.
rows.signals: Popularity: pull_count and star_count from Docker Hub. Trust: images in the mcp/ namespace are built and signed by Docker, with provenance and an SBOM. source.commit pins the code to a commit. run.allowHosts gives a declared network allowlist that a security score can use. Freshness: last_updated and the repository's commit dates. Each entry has a category and tags.
rows.terms: The docker/mcp-registry repository is MIT-licensed, as read on the repository page. Docker Hub API terms were not read in this research.
rows.install: Commands verified today in the Docker docs: 'docker mcp catalog server ls mcp/docker-mcp-catalog', 'docker mcp profile create --name <id>', 'docker mcp profile server add <id> --server <uri>', 'docker mcp profile server remove <id> --name <server>', 'docker mcp profile config <id> --set <server>.<key>=<value>', 'docker mcp client connect <client> --profile <id>' (for example vscode), and 'docker mcp gateway run --profile <id>'. Removing a profile cannot be undone. The list of supported clients was not found in the docs.
rows.notes: This is the best source for security signals: signed images, an SBOM, a pinned commit, an allowlist of network hosts, and declared secrets. The server.yaml files are MIT-licensed and readable through GitHub. The gateway is an alternative install path for agents that Docker supports.

rows.name: awesome-mcp-servers lists (punkpeye, wong2, appcypher) and modelcontextprotocol/servers
rows.what: Curated Markdown lists. punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers has 97,682 stars, an MIT licence, and a last push on 2026-11-06; it holds about 4,633 entries (an approximate count of lines that start with '- ['). Each entry has a GitHub link, often a Glama score badge, and legend emojis: an official implementation, a language, cloud or local service, and the operating system. wong2/awesome-mcp-servers has 4,409 stars, an MIT licence and a last push on 2026-07-13. appcypher/awesome-mcp-servers is archived. modelcontextprotocol/servers holds the reference servers; it has 91,971 stars, its licence shows as NOASSERTION, and its last push was on 2026-11-12.
rows.access: The raw README is at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers/main/README.md, which was tested today. Repository data comes from https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo} without a key, at 60 requests per hour. The lists must be parsed from Markdown.
rows.signals: An official badge, the categories (the list's sections), and the local or cloud marker. The GitHub stars of each linked repository can be fetched separately.
rows.terms: punkpeye's list and wong2's list are MIT-licensed. appcypher's list has no licence and is archived.
rows.install: Not applicable: the lists only link to repositories.
rows.notes: Use these lists only as extra seeds for categories and the 'official' badge, not as a main source.

rows.name: npm download counts API and npm search
rows.what: Download statistics for npm packages, to rank MCP servers whose registry record has packages[].registryType=npm. npm search for keywords:mcp-server reported 11,475 packages today.
rows.access: Tested today: GET https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem returned {downloads: 1351391, start: 2026-11-06, end: 2026-11-12, package}. Bulk requests take up to 128 comma-separated packages, but not scoped packages; a scoped bulk test returned the error 'scoped packages are not currently supported in bulk lookups'. A range request covers at most 18 months, or 365 days in bulk. Per-version counts cover the last 7 days only. Data is processed once a day after UTC midnight. Tested search: GET https://registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search?text=keywords:mcp-server&size=1 returned total, package {name, date}, score {popularity, quality, maintenance}, downloads {weekly, monthly} and dependents. No key is needed. Rate limits are not documented.
rows.signals: Weekly or monthly downloads, dependents, the date of the last publish, and the npm search score.
rows.terms: The download-counts documentation states no API-specific terms; its footer links to the GitHub terms. Reuse terms for the data: not found.
rows.install: Not applicable: these are signals only.
rows.notes: Scoped packages need one request each. Cache the results daily.

rows.name: PyPI download stats (pypistats.org API)
rows.what: Recent download counts for Python MCP server packages, used for records with registryType=pypi.
rows.access: Tested today: GET https://pypistats.org/api/packages/markitdown-mcp/recent returned {data: {last_day: 5144, last_week: 28114, last_month: 109782}}. Other endpoints: overall, python_major, python_minor and system. No key is needed. Rate limits are applied per IP, but the exact limits were not found. Data is updated once a day and kept for 180 days.
rows.signals: Downloads over the last day, week and month.
rows.terms: No formal terms were found. The site's guidance asks users not to download history for every package, to use the BigQuery PyPI tables for bulk work, and to cache results.
rows.install: Not applicable: these are signals only.
rows.notes: Fine for the few thousand PyPI MCP servers with one daily request each. Use BigQuery for anything larger.

research.recommendation:
1. Backbone: the official MCP Registry v0.1. It is open and needs no key. Do one full crawl, then a daily sync with updated_since and version=latest. Drop records with status deleted, and drop remotes on server.smithery.ai and run.tools, which have been dead since 2026-10-31.
2. Shortlist of the best servers: the GitHub MCP Registry, at api.mcp.github.com/v0.1/servers. It has 771 servers in star order, with licence, topics and README, and needs no key. The endpoint is undocumented, so treat it as unstable.
3. Popularity (weight 40): join GitHub stars through repository.url, npm weekly downloads, pypistats, and Docker Hub pull_count.
4. Source reputation (25): the namespace (a verified domain or the publisher's own GitHub organisation), isInOrganization, inclusion in the GitHub list, the Docker mcp/ namespace, and the 'official' badge in punkpeye's list.
5. Freshness (15): updatedAt from the registry, pushedAt from GitHub, the last npm or PyPI publish date, and last_updated on Docker Hub.
6. Security (20): almost no source scans servers upstream. Use your own skill-scan, plus Docker-built signed images with an SBOM, source.commit, allowHosts and declared secrets. Also use the mcpb SHA-256 and the licence.
7. Do not use Glama: it needs a key and its licence forbids competing directories and bulk use. Do not use PulseMCP (private B2B), Smithery (API shut down, no terms) or mcp.so (no API).
8. Install: build commands from packages[] and remotes[]. Docker, through 'docker mcp client connect', offers a second install path. Only the Claude Code commands were verified; other agents are not covered here.
9. Plugin marketplaces were outside this subtask and still need separate research.

rows.name: Claude Code official marketplace (claude-plugins-official)
rows.what: Anthropic's official plugin directory, stored as one marketplace.json file. 316 plugin entries on 2026-11-13. Categories: development 123, productivity 70, database 39, monitoring 22, security 18, deployment 9, design 8, others small, 14 with no category. Built into Claude Code under the reserved name `claude-plugins-official`. The same repo also has a `renames` map (old name to new name). Separate demo marketplace anthropics/claude-code/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (`claude-code-plugins`) has 12 entries.
rows.access: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/main/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (tested 200, 191 KB, no auth). Top-level keys: $schema (https://anthropic.com/claude-code/marketplace.schema.json), name, description, owner, renames, plugins. Entry fields: name, description, source, category (302/316), homepage (300), author (234), plus rare displayName, version, strict, lspServers, skills, tags, keywords. Source types seen: url 163, git-subdir 98, relative path string 54, command 1 (Apple xcode: `xcrun agent plugin path --plugin-format claude`). Example: {name:'42crunch-api-security-testing', category:'security', source:{source:'git-subdir', url:'https://github.com/42Crunch-AI/claude-plugins.git', path:'plugins/api-security-testing', ref:'v1.5.5', sha:'faf53053…'}, homepage:'https://42crunch.com'}. Raw file has no pagination. GitHub REST API is limited to 60 req/h without a token (I hit this limit during research).
rows.signals: Official Anthropic curation. Repo has 47,153 stars and was pushed 2026-11-13. Many git sources are pinned with ref and/or sha, which helps the security check. Popularity comes from the separate stats file (see next row). No per-entry date: freshness has to come from the source repo's commits.
rows.terms: Repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0 (read at raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/main/LICENSE). Each listed plugin keeps its own licence.
rows.install: claude plugin install <name>@claude-plugins-official [-s user|project|local] [--config key=value] [-y] [--json]. claude plugin update <plugin> [-s user|project|local|managed] [-y] [--json]. claude plugin uninstall <plugin> [-s …] [--json]. claude plugin enable|disable <plugin> [-s …] [--json]. claude plugin list. claude plugin marketplace add <owner/repo|path|url>, marketplace remove, marketplace update. claude plugin validate <dir>. For command-source plugins, -y or --accept-command <sha256> is needed when not on a TTY. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference.md
rows.notes: Best plugin backbone: official, machine-readable, licensed, with categories. A `command` source runs a local command at install, so the security check should flag it.

rows.what: Independent community directory of Claude Code skills, MCP servers, plugin marketplaces and plugins. llms.txt (last updated 2026-11-13) claims 23,400+ skills, 8,462+ MCP servers, 3,638+ plugin marketplaces and 17,249+ plugins. Plugins are ranked by marketplace stars. Skill 'best of' pages rank by install-command copies over 90 days. Run by Mert Düzgün and sponsor-funded, with labelled ads.

rows.signals: Marketplace GitHub stars, plugin count per marketplace, install-command copy counts (on-site metric, skills only), categories for skills, MCP and marketplaces. A weekly check removes deleted repos.

rows.install: n/a. It shows native /plugin marketplace add and /plugin install commands.
rows.notes: Good for discovering third-party marketplaces, not usable as a data feed: no API, and the site blocks bots.

3. Install layer: call each agent's native CLI (claude plugin …, copilot plugin …, gemini extensions …, agy plugin …, codex plugin marketplace add), or reuse `npx plugins add -t <target> -y` (7 targets). Cursor and Kiro have no CLI install (UI or deeplink), and Antigravity has no update command.

rows.name: Cisco AI Defense MCP Scanner
rows.what: Python CLI, library and REST API that scans MCP tools, prompts, resources and server instructions. Analyzers: YARA (custom rules allowed), LLM-as-judge, Cisco AI Defense API, behavioral source-code analysis (docstring vs implementation, cross-file dataflow, 10 languages), readiness (20 heuristic rules), prompt defense, vulnerable-package (pip-audit), VirusTotal hash lookup, opt-in schema ($ref) analyzer, and pypi-scan / npm-scan.

Subcommands: remote, stdio, config, known-configs, prompts, resources, instructions, static, behavioral, supplychain, vulnerable-package, virustotal, pypi-scan, npm-scan. Offline: `mcp-scanner static --tools tools.json [--prompts ..] [--resources ..]` scans pre-exported JSON without a live server. Examples: `mcp-scanner --scan-known-configs --analyzers yara --format summary`; `mcp-scanner --stdio-command uvx --stdio-arg=--from --stdio-arg=mcp-server-fetch ... --analyzers yara`. No key is needed for YARA, readiness, prompt-defense, vulnerable-package and static YARA. The LLM and behavioral analyzers need an LLM key (a local Ollama works with a placeholder key). The AI Defense API and VirusTotal need their own keys.
rows.signals: Latest release 4.8.7 (2026-10-20); 1118 stars; last push 2026-11-12; maintained by Cisco.
rows.terms: Apache-2.0 (verified via the GitHub API). Can be bundled or invoked from a free tool.

rows.notes: Best offline, no-account option for MCP. Skill Advisor can export tools/list JSON once, or take descriptions from registry metadata, then run `static` with YARA. Only the YARA, static and readiness paths are offline.

rows.name: Checks Skill Advisor can do itself STATICALLY (no server run, no account)
rows.what:
1. Identity: registry namespace vs repo owner; remote URL host vs namespace domain; package repository field == server.json repository == provenance sourceRepository; typosquat distance to known names.
2. Supply chain: npm/PyPI provenance present and verified (deps.dev slsaProvenances.verified); OSV/GHSA advisories and MAL- entries; minimum safe versions; licence present; deprecation and status (deleted, deprecated).
3. Pinning: rewrite installs to exact versions (npx -y pkg@x.y.z, uvx pkg==x.y.z, docker image@sha256); flag unpinned npx/uvx/@latest and git branches; for plugins, require ref+sha, then after checkout verify HEAD==sha and reject 40-hex ref names (Plugin4Shell).
4. Command review (MCP spec): show the full command; flag sudo, rm -rf, curl|sh, base64, eval, network fetch at start, paths in ~/.ssh, ~/.aws or hidden home dirs (SANDWORM ~/.dev-utils), env overrides (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL etc.).
5. Plugin manifest: list hooks (especially SessionStart), MCP servers, bin/LSP, `command`/`archive`/`npm` sources, enableAllProjectMcpServers/enabledMcpjsonServers; npm install scripts (postinstall).
6. Text checks on descriptions available without running (registry description, README, skill/agent markdown, Docker catalog tools list): <IMPORTANT>-style hidden instructions, references to other tools (shadowing), sensitive paths, 'do not tell the user', zero-width/homoglyph/base64 normalisation before matching (Ramparts approach); optional offline YARA through `mcp-scanner static`.
7. Remote servers: https only; block private, link-local and metadata IPs; domain age or allowlist; declared OAuth scopes when present (flag *, all, admin).
8. Drift: store a hash per installed config, package version and description set; alert on unknown MCP entries in agent configs and on any change after approval (MCPoison, rug pull).
9. Trust bonus: listed in docker/mcp-registry with commit pin; official namespace (io.github.<vendor> / vendor domain).
rows.access: n/a
rows.signals: Cisco skill-scanner benchmark: rules alone catch 7.7% of malicious skills, so a static pass is only 'no known pattern', never 'safe'.
rows.terms: n/a
rows.install: n/a
rows.notes: All sources needed (official MCP registry, npm/PyPI JSON, deps.dev, OSV, GitHub advisories) were tested without a key today.

rows.name: Checks that NEED running or connecting to the server
rows.what:
1. Real tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list and server instructions (the descriptions the model actually sees; they may differ from the README or registry).
2. Rug-pull baseline: hash of live descriptions at approval, re-fetched on every update or session (TOFU like mcp-context-protector).
3. Bait-and-switch: compare answers under different client names (MCP-Shield --identify-as).
4. Toxic-flow analysis across all installed servers (private-data source + untrusted input + exfil sink), which needs the live tool set.
5. OAuth behaviour of remote servers: actual authorization_endpoint and scheme (CVE-2025-6514), requested scopes, redirect targets, SSRF attempts.
6. Behaviour: network egress, file access outside the declared roots, spawned processes. This needs a sandbox or container (Docker MCP gateway, or the agent-scan --dangerously-run-mcp-servers CI mode).
7. Behavioral source analysis with an LLM (Cisco behavioral, Snyk API). This needs a key or an account and is optional.
rows.access: Run only in a sandbox, only after explicit user consent, with the exact command shown (MCP spec MUST).
rows.signals: Tools that do this: Cisco mcp-scanner (stdio/remote, YARA offline), Ramparts, Snyk Agent Scan (account), MCP-Shield (stale).
rows.terms: n/a
rows.install: n/a
rows.notes: Starting a stdio server executes its code. Never do it implicitly during browsing or scoring.

research.recommendation:
1. Identity backbone: the official MCP Registry API (no key, server.json with exact package versions and runtimeHint). It proves only namespace ownership and does not scan.
2. Trust signals for the daily job, all free and keyless (tested today): npm attestations, the PyPI Integrity API, deps.dev (verified SLSA, advisories, licence, stars), OSV plus GitHub Advisories (CVE and malware), and docker/mcp-registry (commit pin plus agentic audit, MIT).
3. Skip Glama: its API needs a key and per-page attribution. Skip Smithery scores: their current state is unknown and its API needs a key. OpenSSF Scorecard: use only when present.
4. Security score: compute it locally. Static checks cover identity and repo match, provenance, advisories, pinning (rewrite to exact versions, Plugin4Shell HEAD==sha check), command and hook review, normalised text rules on descriptions, and drift hashes.
5. Optional offline engine: Cisco mcp-scanner (Apache-2.0, `static` plus YARA, no key). cc-audit (MIT, offline) is optional for plugins and hooks.
6. Snyk Agent Scan stays opt-in only, because it needs an account, sends data to Snyk and runs servers. Treat Nova-Proximity (GPL-3.0) as external only; mcp-context-protector is archived and MCP-Shield is stale.
7. Live-description scanning, rug-pull TOFU and toxic-flow analysis need the server running. Do them only in a sandbox, with explicit consent and the full command shown.
8. Display rule: a static pass means 'no known pattern found', never 'safe'. Cisco measured that rules alone catch 7.7% of malicious skills.
9. Incidents to encode: postmark-mcp (unpinned rug pull), SANDWORM_MODE (injected config entries), Check Point (project hooks and env overrides), Plugin4Shell (pin bypass), CVE minimum versions.

checked.name: Smithery security scans
checked.claim: Smithery announced Invariant MCP-Scan on every listed server on 2025-04-24; server pages 404; registry API returns HTTP 500 without a key; terms unknown.
checked.correction: The announcement is verified: dated 2025-04-24, it says all Smithery servers are scanned by MCP-Scan, with results on each server's registry page. The access claim is wrong today. A GET to https://registry.smithery.ai/servers?pageSize=1 returned HTTP 200 without a key, reporting totalCount 20750 and totalPages 500. List items carry the fields verified, useCount, remote, isDeployed, bySmithery, createdAt and score; score was null on every item sampled. The detail endpoint https://registry.smithery.ai/servers/{qualifiedName} also returned 200 without a key. It has a `security` field, but the field was null on all 6 servers sampled (brave, slack, googledrive and others). So scans are not exposed as usable data today. There is a 'verified' boolean in the API, which contradicts the secondary claim that there is no verified badge. Terms not found: smithery.ai/terms returns 404. A site banner says Smithery's MCP Proxy and managed identity shut down on October 31 (reported, from a search snippet).

checked.name: Incident (malicious, in the wild, IDE extension not agent plugin): trojanized Claude Code extension on Cursor marketplace
checked.claim: 2026-10-29; tampered 2.1.313 on Cursor marketplace ~11 h; loader prepended to extension.js, SSH key svc-telemetry, reverse tunnel, persistence; up to 5,000 exposed; VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX and npm unaffected; 2.1.314 published.
checked.correction: BleepingComputer (dated 2026-10-30) confirms: version 2.1.313, a window of about 02:27 to 13:35 PT on Oct 29 (about 11 h), and a loader prepended to extension.js. Cursor shut its marketplace temporarily to audit and rotate keys. The article does not name a fixed version. A secondary blog reports 2.1.314 on GitHub and npm on 2026-10-30 and says 2.1.313 is absent from the npm records and the changelog. Treat '2.1.314 is the fix' as reported.

checked.claim: mcp-remote CVE-2025-6514 9.6, 0.0.5–0.1.15, fixed 0.1.16; Inspector CVE-2025-49596 9.4 fixed 0.14.1; filesystem CVE-2025-53109/53110 fixed 0.6.3 / 2025.7.1; mcp-server-git CVE-2025-68143/68144/68145 fixed 2025.12.18; Cursor CVE-2025-54136 fixed 1.3; Smithery traversal 2025-06-13/15. rows.name: add-mcp (CLI + Node library)
rows.what: Open-source CLI and library that writes one canonical MCP server config into the native config file of 25 agents: Antigravity, Cline, Cline CLI, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Factory Droid, fx, Gemini CLI, Goose, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build, Hermes, Junie, Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Kiro CLI, Mastra Code, MCPorter, OpenCode, Pi, VS Code, Windsurf and Zed. Commands: implicit add, find/search, list, remove, sync/unify, list-agents. npm version 2.6.1 (npm modified 2026-11-01).
rows.access: CLI: `npx add-mcp <url|package|"command"> [-a agent]... [-g] [-y] [--all] [-n name] [-t http|sse] [--header 'K: V'] [--env K=V] [--timeout ms] [--scopes a,b] [--auto-approve [--approve-tool t]] [--gitignore]`. Other commands: `npx add-mcp find <kw> -a claude-code -g -y`, `list [-g] [-a]`, `remove <name|url|pkg> [-g] [-a] -y`, `sync -g -y`. Library (ESM): `upsertServer(agent, name, {type:'http',url}|{command,args,env}, {local:true,cwd})`, `removeServer(agent, name, opts)`, `listInstalledServers({cwd}|{global:true})`, `detectProjectAgents(cwd)`, `detectGlobalAgents()`. upsertServer and removeServer return `{success, path, error?}` and do not throw. The find command sends GET `<registry>?version=latest&limit=100&search=<kw>&source=cli`. Default registry: https://add-mcp.com/registry/api/v1/servers. Optional registry: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers, configured in ~/.config/add-mcp/config.json under `findRegistries`.
rows.signals: GitHub neon-solutions/add-mcp: 321 stars, last push 2026-11-01, Apache-2.0 (GitHub API, read today). Maintained under the Neon org. The default registry is generated from integrations.sh plus registry.overlay.json.
rows.terms: Apache-2.0 (npm metadata and GitHub API, read today). The licence of add-mcp registry data (integrations.sh) was not found.
rows.install: Registry server.json to config mapping, read in src/find.ts and src/installer.ts today: (1) The entry needs name, description and version. Only `packages[]` with registryType `npm` are used, so pypi, oci, nuget and mcpb packages are dropped. Entries with neither an npm package nor remotes are skipped. (2) With `-y`, a remote is chosen over a package, and streamable-http over sse. (3) A remote maps to `{type: http|sse, url}`. Required URL variables and required headers get placeholder values under -y. (4) A package maps to `command: "npx", args: ["-y", <identifier>, ...packageArguments]`. The registry `version` is NOT written, so the package floats unpinned. Required environmentVariables get placeholders. (5) The server name comes from the lowercased title, or else from the name with 'mcp' and 'com' removed. (6) `find <kw> -y` installs the FIRST hit (`visibleEntries[0]`) without a prompt. Per-OS global paths: Windows %APPDATA%\Code\User, macOS ~/Library/Application Support, Linux $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config (src/agents.ts).
rows.notes: Best fit for Skill Advisor: import the library in-process, with no child process, so the Windows .cmd problem does not arise. Without `-a` and with `-y`, the CLI writes to ALL detected agents. With no agent detected, it writes to all project-capable agents. Always pass explicit `-a`. `-y` writes placeholder secrets (e.g. `<your-header-value-here>`), so collect real values first. Exit codes from source: 0 on success, 1 on error (process.exit(1) or exitCode=1). No --json output flag was found in the README. --auto-approve writes Claude permission rules to .claude/settings.local.json or ~/.claude/settings.json, and Codex approval_mode. .mcp.json is shared by Claude Code and Copilot CLI, so removing a server for one agent removes it for both. add-mcp does not wrap npx in `cmd /c` on Windows: no 'cmd' string found in the source.
rows.source: https://github.com/neon-solutions/add-mcp (README, src/find.ts, src/installer.ts, src/agents.ts, src/lib.ts); https://registry.npmjs.org/add-mcp

rows.name: Claude Code: claude mcp
rows.what: Native Claude Code subcommands for MCP servers: add, add-json, add-from-claude-desktop, list, get, remove, reset-project-choices, login, logout.
rows.access: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> [--header 'K: V'] [-s local|project|user]`. `claude mcp add [--env K=V] --transport stdio <name> -- <cmd> [args...]`. Everything after `--` goes to the server. Do not put the server name right after `--env`. `claude mcp add-json <name> '<json>'`. `claude mcp remove <name>`. `claude mcp list`. `claude mcp get <name>`. `claude mcp login <name> [--no-browser]`. Short flags: -t, -e, -H, -s. OAuth flags: --callback-port, --client-id, --client-secret.
rows.signals: Official Anthropic docs, read today.
rows.terms: Claude Code is proprietary under Anthropic terms (reported; terms page not read).
rows.install: Scopes and storage: local (default) in ~/.claude.json under the project path; project in .mcp.json at the project root; user in ~/.claude.json. Precedence: local, then project, then user, then plugin, then claude.ai connectors. In interactive sessions, project .mcp.json servers need user approval. In `claude -p` or SDK runs they load without asking.
rows.notes: No `mcp update` command and no documented --json flag for mcp add, list or remove were found. Updating means remove plus add, or rewriting the file. Exit codes for `claude mcp` were not found. The docs no longer mention the old `cmd /c npx` Windows note (not found on page). On Windows, Claude Code ships as a native claude.exe (install.ps1, install.cmd, or winget Anthropic.ClaudeCode), so spawn('claude', args) works without a shell. If it was installed through npm, it is a .cmd shim (reported).

rows.name: Gemini CLI: gemini mcp
rows.what: Gemini CLI subcommands for mcpServers in settings.json: add, list, remove, enable, disable. Latest release v0.68.0, 2026-11-10.

rows.name: How MCP server updates work (npx, pinned, remote)
rows.what: Update semantics for configured MCP servers. No agent has an 'mcp update' command, so an update is either a config rewrite or a re-resolve at the next launch.
rows.access: npm docs (CLI v11): `-y/--yes` suppresses the install prompt. Names without a specifier match whatever version is in the local project. Packages not installed locally go into the npm cache. A specifier matches only with the exact same name and version.
rows.signals: npm docs v11 (11.21.2 shown, page edited 2025-10-05).
rows.terms: n/a
rows.install: Stdio from npm: `npx -y pkg` (what add-mcp writes) floats. Whether a re-run picks up a newer release or reuses the npx cache is NOT stated in the docs (unknown). `pkg@latest` (VS Code's example uses @playwright/mcp@latest) asks for the dist-tag on each launch, but cache reuse is again not documented. `pkg@1.2.3` is fully pinned, and updating it means rewriting args through upsertServer or remove plus add. Remote (http/sse) servers are updated server-side, with nothing to do locally. Plugin-bundled servers update with the plugin.
rows.notes: For Skill Advisor's update and security model: store the pinned version from registry `packages[].version` and write `pkg@version` yourself, because add-mcp drops the version. An update then becomes a visible, diffable config change. The exact npx caching behaviour with @latest is unknown.

rows.name: Claude Code: claude plugin and claude plugin marketplace
rows.what: Shell commands to install and manage Claude Code plugins from marketplaces: install(i), uninstall, enable, disable, update, list, details, configure, prune, init, validate, eval, plus marketplace add, list, remove(rm) and update.
rows.access: `claude plugin marketplace add <owner/repo[#ref|@ref]|git-url|https-url-to-marketplace.json|./path> [--scope user|project|local] [--sparse paths...] [--json]`. `claude plugin install <name@marketplace> [-s user|project|local] [-y] [--accept-command <sha256>] [--json]`. In one step: `claude plugin install <name> --marketplace <source>`, which needs v2.1.292 or later. `claude plugin uninstall <id> [-s] [--keep-data] [--json]`. `claude plugin enable|disable <id> [-s] [--json]`. `claude plugin disable -a`. `claude plugin update <id> [-s user|project|local|managed] [-y] [--json]`. `claude plugin list --json [--available]`. `claude plugin marketplace update [name] [--json]`. `claude plugin marketplace remove <name> [--scope] [--json]`.
rows.signals: Official docs, read today. The official marketplace is anthropics/claude-plugins-official. Auto-update is on by default for official marketplace names and off for third-party ones.
rows.terms: Claude Code is proprietary (reported). Each marketplace has its own licence.
rows.install: Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on failure (validate adds 2). --json prints ONE JSON object on the LAST stdout line, always with {command, outcome: ok|failed, message}, plus pluginId, scope, failureCode, alreadyInGoalState and similar. Where results are recorded: enabledPlugins in the scope's settings file (~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json). Marketplaces go to extraKnownMarketplaces in user settings. The plugins root ~/.claude/plugins/ ($CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR) holds known_marketplaces.json, installed_plugins.json (scope, installPath, version), marketplaces/<name>/ and the cache.
rows.notes: Gotchas: (1) For a command-source or headersHelper plugin without a TTY, install is refused with exit 1 unless you pass -y (v2.1.229+) or --accept-command. -y is IGNORED when run from inside a Claude session (Bash tool or hook). (2) enable or disable on a plugin already in that state exits 1, so treat `alreadyInGoalState: true` as success. (3) `marketplace remove` from the last scope uninstalls all of that marketplace's plugins and deletes their data. Use `marketplace update` instead to refresh. (4) `marketplace update` with no name refreshes listings but does not upgrade installed plugins. (5) Minimum versions: --json 2.1.268+ (marketplace --json 2.1.287+). (6) On a fresh machine, add anthropics/claude-plugins-official before installing. The Windows binary is native claude.exe (reported for the npm variant).

rows.name: Gemini CLI: gemini extensions
rows.what: Extension manager for Gemini CLI: install, uninstall, enable, disable, update, new, link, config. The public gallery is at geminicli.com/extensions/browse.
rows.access: `gemini extensions install <github-url|local-path> [--ref <ref>] [--auto-update] [--pre-release] [--consent] [--skip-settings]`. `gemini extensions uninstall <name...>`. `gemini extensions update <name>`. `gemini extensions update --all`. `gemini extensions enable|disable <name> [--scope user|workspace]`. `gemini extensions config <name> [setting] [--scope]`.
rows.signals: Official repo docs and source, read today. v0.68.0 released 2026-11-10.
rows.terms: Gemini CLI is Apache-2.0 (reported). Licences of gallery extensions vary.
rows.install: Non-interactive use needs `--consent` (auto-accepts the security consent) and `--skip-settings` (skips the settings prompts). Installs are copied to ~/.gemini/extensions/<name>. Changes take effect after a CLI restart. These commands do not work in interactive mode. Git must be installed for GitHub sources.
rows.notes: From source (packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/install.ts): installing from an UNTRUSTED LOCAL FOLDER still prompts 'Do you trust this folder… [y/N]' even with --consent. Pre-trust the folder or install from a git URL. Any error leads to process.exit(1). Without --consent, the code prompts '[Y/n]' on stdin. Updates pull from the source to the version in gemini-extension.json, and --auto-update turns on automatic updates. The npm install gives gemini.cmd on Windows (reported).

rows.name: GitHub Copilot CLI: copilot plugin
rows.what: Copilot CLI plugin manager: install(add), uninstall(remove, rm), list, update, enable, disable, plus marketplace add, list, browse, update(refresh) and remove. The default marketplace is awesome-copilot, built in and not removable. github/copilot-plugins is no longer a default and must be added.
rows.access: `copilot plugin install <plugin@marketplace|OWNER/REPO|OWNER/REPO:PATH|git-url|./path>`. `copilot plugin uninstall <name>`. `copilot plugin list [--json]` returns a flat array of {name, marketplace?, version?, enabled, source, installedFrom?}. `copilot plugin update <name>`. `copilot plugin update --all`. `copilot plugin enable|disable <name>`. `copilot plugin marketplace add <owner/repo[#ref]|url|path>`. `copilot plugin marketplace browse <name> [--json]`. `copilot plugin marketplace update [name]`. `copilot plugin marketplace remove <name> [--force]`.
rows.signals: Official GitHub Docs reference, read today.
rows.terms: Copilot CLI is proprietary (reported).
rows.install: Storage: ~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>, or _direct/<source-id> for direct installs. Marketplace cache: ~/.cache/copilot/marketplaces (Linux) or ~/Library/Caches/copilot/marketplaces (macOS), overridable with COPILOT_CACHE_HOME. Manifests: plugin.json at the root (Agent Plugins schema) wins over .plugin/, .github/plugin/ and .claude-plugin/plugin.json. marketplace.json is searched in this order: root, .plugin/, .github/plugin/, .claude-plugin/.
rows.notes: No --yes flag and no exit codes were documented. Whether install prompts without a TTY is unknown. `marketplace remove` is refused while plugins from it are installed, unless you pass --force (which uninstalls them). VS Code auto-discovers plugins from ~/.copilot/installed-plugins. The vercel `plugins` CLI notes that direct local-path installs are deprecated and registers a marketplace first. --config-dir is deprecated, so use COPILOT_HOME.

rows.name: Antigravity CLI: agy plugin
rows.what: Plugin manager of the Antigravity CLI. The official marketplace is antigravity-plugins-official. Plugins bundle skills, MCP servers, agents, rules and hooks.
rows.access: `agy plugin install firebase@antigravity-plugins-official`. `agy plugin install <name>` (a bare name means the official marketplace). `agy plugin install https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`. `agy plugin install </path/to/local/plugin>`. `agy plugin list [--json]`. `agy plugin enable|disable|uninstall <name>`. `agy plugin validate --strict`.
rows.signals: Official antigravity.google docs page (no date or version shown). Vendors such as Sonar and Endor Labs publish agy install lines.
rows.terms: Proprietary Google product (reported).
rows.install: Local folders are 'staged into your profile'. The exact path was not found on the page. `agy plugin import gemini` converts Gemini CLI extensions (reported, from community and vendor sources).
rows.notes: update, import and link subcommands, the --yes, --consent and --scope flags, and exit codes were not found on the official page. Some installs expose the binary as `antigravity` instead of `agy` (reported, Endor Labs). Windows binary form unknown.

rows.name: Codex CLI: codex plugin
rows.what: Codex plugin commands: add, list, remove, plus marketplace add, list, upgrade and remove. Plugins bundle skills, mcp.json, assets and hooks. The manifest is a root plugin.json (Agent Plugins schema), with .codex-plugin/plugin.json as a fallback.
rows.access: `codex plugin marketplace add <owner/repo[@ref]|git-url|ssh-url|./root> [--ref REF] [--sparse PATH]... [--json]` (JSON: marketplaceName, installedRoot, alreadyAdded). `codex plugin add <plugin[@marketplace]> [-m NAME] [--json]` (JSON: pluginId, name, marketplaceName, version, installedPath, authPolicy). `codex plugin list [-m NAME] [--json] [--available --json]` (installed and available arrays). `codex plugin remove <plugin[@marketplace]> [-m] [--json]`. `codex plugin marketplace upgrade [name] [--json]`. `codex plugin marketplace remove <name> [--json]`.
rows.signals: Official OpenAI docs, read today.
rows.terms: Codex CLI is Apache-2.0 (reported).
rows.install: Cache: ~/.codex/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/. Enabling is in config.toml: `[plugins."name@marketplace"] enabled = true|false`, in the user file or the project .codex/config.toml (trusted projects only). Marketplace files: $REPO_ROOT/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json or ~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json.
rows.notes: No `codex plugin update` and no enable/disable command were found. Update by running `marketplace upgrade` (during refresh Codex can install or refresh files for configured plugins) or by re-running add. Disable by editing config.toml. Exit codes not documented. The plugin's authPolicy may need a sign-in at install time. Hooks only work for manually installed desktop plugins. In the TUI, /plugins browses plugins. codex.cmd shim on Windows (reported).

rows.name: Cursor plugins (no shell install)
rows.what: Cursor Marketplace and team marketplaces for plugins. Manifests: .cursor-plugin/plugin.json, or a root plugin.json (Agent Plugins standard, agent-plugins.org). Multi-plugin repos use .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json.
rows.access: Install through Customize or the Marketplace (Install, then choose project or user scope). The in-chat `/add-plugin <name>` or `/add-plugin <github-url>` is reported by vendor docs (Svelte, Railway) and the Cursor forum, not by the official docs page. The only deeplink documented is for MCP, not for plugins.
rows.signals: Official docs read today. Teams plans get one team marketplace, Enterprise unlimited. Install modes: Default Off, Default On, Required. Auto Refresh re-indexes at most every 10 minutes.
rows.terms: Proprietary (reported).
rows.install: No non-interactive shell command was found. A Cursor forum thread reports that no `cursor-agent plugin install` exists. Local development folder: ~/.cursor/plugins/local/<plugin>. The vercel `plugins` CLI targets Cursor (detects `cursor` or `cursor-agent`); its install path for Cursor was not checked.
rows.notes: Uninstall and disable were not described on the docs page. Required plugins cannot be uninstalled. A forum bug reports that URL installs through /add-plugin stay pinned to stale commits. For Skill Advisor: offer a guided UI step, or write the local plugin folder plus config (path unverified), rather than a CLI call.

rows.name: VS Code agent plugins (Preview)
rows.what: VS Code agent plugins are bundles of skills, agents, MCP servers and hooks, gated by the `chat.plugins.enabled` setting. Marketplaces are configured in `chat.plugins.marketplaces` (experimental).
rows.access: UI: Agent Customizations editor, or Chat: Install Plugin from Source. Deeplinks: `vscode://chat-plugin/install?source=<url-encoded owner/repo>&plugin=<name>` and `vscode://chat-plugin/add-marketplace?ref=<source>`. Both ALWAYS ask for confirmation.
rows.signals: Official VS Code docs, dated 11/11/2026, Preview.
rows.terms: Microsoft (reported).
rows.install: No shell install command was found. VS Code auto-discovers plugins installed by Copilot CLI in ~/.copilot/installed-plugins/. The vercel `plugins` CLI writes a staged local copy into the user settings key `chat.pluginLocations` (read in its bundle).
rows.notes: The simplest non-interactive route is `copilot plugin install`, which VS Code then picks up, or a `chat.pluginLocations` entry. The first install from a new marketplace shows a trust prompt.

rows.name: npx plugins (vercel-labs/plugins)
rows.what: CLI that installs open-plugin or Agent Plugins format repos into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Grok Build, Kimi Code, Copilot CLI and VS Code. It translates the plugin to each tool and calls the tool's native system. npm version 1.3.6 (npm modified 2026-10-30).
rows.access: `npx plugins add <owner/repo|https|ssh|./path> [-t target] [-s user|project|local] [-y]`. `npx plugins discover <source>` is a dry run. `npx plugins targets` lists detected tools. Repos are shallow-cloned to ~/.cache/plugins/<slug>. Discovery order: marketplace.json, then the root plugin, then a recursive scan 2 levels deep.
rows.signals: Vercel Labs project. Zero runtime dependencies, Node 18+. Star count not retrieved (GitHub API rate-limited).
rows.terms: The README says Apache 2.0, but package.json has NO license field and the LICENSE file was not read, so treat it as unverified.
rows.install: From the bundle (dist/index.js, read today): Codex uses spawnSync('codex', ['plugin','add',ref]). Copilot uses `copilot plugin marketplace add`, then `install plugin@mkt`. Claude Code uses execSync of a string `${claude} plugin install "ref" --scope` only for the vercel plugin. Otherwise it writes ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json itself. VS Code gets a chat.pluginLocations entry. Grok uses `grok plugin install … --trust`. It also uses `which claude`, which is not Windows-friendly.
rows.notes: Install only: there is NO remove, update or list command. Telemetry is ON by default and goes to telemetry.labs.vercel.dev; set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1. Scopes other than user only work for vercel/vercel-plugin on Claude. Not suitable as Skill Advisor's backend. Use it as a reference for the per-agent translation only.

rows.name: Spawning agent CLIs from Node without a shell (macOS, Linux, Windows)
rows.what: Constraints for calling `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `copilot`, `agy`, `code` and `npx` from Skill Advisor with spawn(cmd, argsArray).
rows.access: Node docs (v26.13.1): on Windows, .bat and .cmd files cannot run through execFile. Call them with spawn plus `shell` (not recommended, DEP0190), with exec, or with `spawn('cmd.exe', ['/c', 'x.cmd', ...])`. Node security release (April 2024, CVE-2024-27980): spawn and spawnSync now throw EINVAL for .bat or .cmd without `shell`. The fix was applied to the 18.x, 20.x and 21.x lines.
rows.signals: Official nodejs.org pages, read today.
rows.terms: n/a
rows.install: macOS and Linux: spawn('claude', [...]) with an argument array works directly. Windows: resolve the full path first (`where.exe <name>`). For a .exe (native Claude Code, claude.exe), spawn it directly. For an npm shim (npx.cmd, codex.cmd, gemini.cmd, copilot.cmd, code.cmd), use spawn('cmd.exe', ['/d','/s','/c', fullPath, ...args]) with strictly validated arguments, or avoid the spawn entirely. Spawning a bare 'codex' without an extension on Windows is not resolved to codex.cmd (reported; libuv only tries .com and .exe, PATHEXT not mentioned in the Node docs).
rows.notes: Best practice for Skill Advisor: (1) For MCP, use the add-mcp library in-process, with no spawn. (2) For plugins, run native CLIs with argument arrays and their --json flags (Claude, Codex, Copilot list) and parse only the last stdout line for Claude. (3) Never interpolate user strings into a shell command line. The vercel `plugins` CLI uses execSync with string templates, which is the anti-pattern.

research.recommendation:
MCP: use the add-mcp library (Apache-2.0, v2.6.1) in-process. upsertServer, removeServer and listInstalledServers cover 25 agents with the correct per-OS paths and no child process, so the Windows .cmd and EINVAL problem does not arise. Do not use its `-y` or `find` behaviour as is. Build the config yourself from server.json, because add-mcp drops the version, keeps only npm packages, writes placeholder secrets and picks the first search hit. Pin `pkg@version` so that an update is an explicit, scored config rewrite. Remote servers need no local update.
Catalogue backbone for MCP: the official MCP Registry (/v0.1/servers, gives status, publishedAt, updatedAt, isLatest) plus the curated add-mcp registry for canonical vendor entries. Neither gives popularity, so add GitHub and npm signals as you do for skills.
Plugins: call each native CLI with an argument array, never a shell string. Claude: `plugin marketplace add` then `plugin install name@mkt -s <scope> --json`, plus enable, disable, update and uninstall with --json. Treat alreadyInGoalState as success. Codex: `plugin marketplace add`, `plugin add|remove --json`, `marketplace upgrade`; enable means editing config.toml. Copilot: `plugin install`, `update` and `uninstall`; VS Code picks those installs up automatically. Gemini: `extensions install <git-url> --consent --skip-settings`. Antigravity: `agy plugin install`.
Cursor and VS Code have no shell install for plugins: offer a deeplink or UI step, or the Copilot route for VS Code. Avoid `npx plugins` as a backend: it can only install, has telemetry on by default and its licence is unverified.

checked.name: Antigravity MCP (file only)
checked.claim: Antigravity IDE and agy CLI share one global MCP file, ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, and nothing else (global only, per add-mcp). There is no `agy mcp add` command. Plugin-bundled MCP servers are exposed as `<plugin>_<server>`. Install with `npx add-mcp <src> -a antigravity -g -y`.
checked.correction: The global path is right and is now verified on the official Antigravity docs. It is ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\mcp_config.json), and the IDE and CLI docs both name it. 'Global only' is wrong for Antigravity itself. The official docs also define a workspace file, <workspace>/.agents/mcp_config.json, which 'applies only to that workspace'. Only add-mcp's agent table is global-only (Project path '-'), so add-mcp cannot write the workspace file and Skill Advisor would have to write it itself. The App surface names no path: the docs say to use 'Copy Config File Path'. File format: root `mcpServers`; stdio uses `command` and `args`; remote uses `serverUrl` (`url` is also accepted). No `agy mcp add` command is documented; the CLI way is the interactive `/mcp` manager, or editing the JSON by hand. The `<plugin-name>_<server-name>` namespacing is verified on the marketplace page. Older third-party guides still cite ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json, which may be a legacy path (reported). The add-mcp flags -a/--agent, -g/--global and -y/--yes are verified in the README. The `upsertServer` function is exported by the add-mcp package (README `import { upsertServer } from "add-mcp"`). add-mcp latest on npm is 2.6.1 (registry GET today).

checked.name: How MCP server updates work (npx, pinned, remote)
checked.claim: npm docs (CLI v11): -y suppresses the prompt; unspecified names match the local project version; non-local packages go into the npm cache; a specifier matches only on exact name+version. Whether re-runs pick up newer releases or @latest reuses the cache is undocumented. No agent has an 'mcp update' command. add-mcp drops the version (source: installer.ts).
checked.correction: The quoted npx semantics are verified, but cite the current docs. npm latest is 12.2.2 (registry dist-tags, GET today). v11 (11.21.2) is now labelled 'Legacy' on docs.npmjs.com. The v12 npx page (12.2.2, last edited 2025-10-05) has the same text on -y/--yes, specifier matching, and the npm-cache folder added to PATH. It is equally silent on @latest resolution and cache reuse, so 'unknown' stays correct. The VS Code example `npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest` is verified on the VS Code MCP servers page, which describes no update procedure (only disable, uninstall and stop). The 'add-mcp drops the version' claim is mis-attributed and too broad. installer.ts writes `args: ["-y", parsed.value, ...]`, and source-parser.ts keeps the raw input in `value`; it strips @version only for the inferred server name. So a direct `npx add-mcp pkg@1.2.3` keeps the pin. The version is dropped only on the `find`/`search` path: src/find.ts `formatPackageTarget` returns `pkg.identifier` and ignores the registry `version`. Change the source to src/find.ts and narrow the claim to installs from the registry. 'No agent has an mcp update command' was not checked across the 78 agents: unverifiable as a universal statement. The recommendation to write `pkg@version` yourself from registry `packages[].version` stays sound.

checked.name: Cursor plugins (no shell install)
checked.claim: Manifests .cursor-plugin/plugin.json or root plugin.json (agent-plugins.org); marketplace.json for multi-plugin repos; install via Customize/Marketplace with project or user scope; /add-plugin is reported only by vendors and the forum; only MCP deeplinks; Teams 1 marketplace, Enterprise unlimited; modes Default Off/On/Required; Auto Refresh at most every 10 min; local folder ~/.cursor/plugins/local/<plugin>; no non-interactive shell command; stale-commit bug on URL installs.
checked.correction: Most facts are verified on cursor.com/docs/plugins today (the page shows no date). Manifest paths, Customize > Install > project/user scope, and the MCP-only deeplink `cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=$NAME&config=$BASE64_ENCODED_CONFIG` are all confirmed. Teams get 1 team marketplace (Default not counted); Enterprise is unlimited, admin-only. The three install modes are confirmed, and Required plugins cannot be uninstalled. Auto Refresh re-indexes at most every 10 minutes, needs the Cursor GitHub App, and running Cloud Agents keep their starting versions. Local folder ~/.cursor/plugins/local is verified: restart, or run Developer: Reload Window. On Enterprise, 'Allow Local Plugin Imports' is off by default, which Skill Advisor must warn about. The docs page gives no uninstall or disable steps for plugins. /add-plugin: the Svelte docs show `/add-plugin svelte` (vendor, reported). The forum thread does NOT mention /add-plugin, so drop it as a source for that claim. Add the CLI detail from that thread. `cursor-agent plugin marketplace add` exists. Inside `cursor-agent`, typing `/plugin` opens an interactive Marketplace tab with user/project scope. A responder who appears to be Cursor staff (deanrie, 2026-07-19) said there is no non-interactive `cursor-agent plugin install <plugin-id>` yet. User-scope plugins installed in the IDE or Dashboard sync to the CLI. The stale-commit bug is reported in separate forum threads, with staff acknowledgment and no ETA. It also hits CLI `plugin marketplace update`, which reports 0 plugins indexed (reported). The vercel `plugins` CLI claim was not checked: unknown. Licence 'proprietary' was not checked: unknown.
